sources.name: YouGov Ratings: most popular rap & hip-hop music artists (US), Q2 2026
sources.method: Share with a positive opinion, top 20 only. Re-sorted to solo rappers (groups and non-rappers like Pharrell, Post Malone and Jelly Roll removed): Eminem, Ice Cube, LL, 50 Cent, Tupac, MC Hammer, Dre, Ludacris, Missy, Kendrick, Biggie, Pitbull.

sources.name: Celebrity Family Feud best-rapper survey (100 people), top 8 answers: Snoop, 2Pac, Eminem, Dr. Dre, LL, Biggie, 50 Cent, Jay-Z
sources.method: Reused from prior file; same top 8 and order seen again in Complex and The Source search snippets (2024). The HipHopDX page itself was not re-fetched.

sources.name: Spotify most-streamed artists of all time (kworb)
sources.method: Rapper-only ordinals from total streams, read 2026-10-07; capped at 35. Jay-Z does not appear in this list at all (unexplained), so Spotify is excluded from his average.

sources.name: Commercial composite (counted as ONE source): rapper-only order within RIAA highest-certified US artists, Billboard Greatest of All Time Billboard 200 artists, Billboard GOAT Hot 100 artists, Wikipedia worldwide certified units
sources.method: Mean of rapper-only positions (missing = list length + 5), then re-ranked among the 10 rappers present. Other URLs: https://www.billboard.com/charts/greatest-of-all-time-artists/ ; https://www.billboard.com/charts/greatest-hot-100-artists/ ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_best-selling_music_artists

sources.name: YouGov poll of US adults rating the music of Billboard's top 20 rappers (net love/like minus dislike/hate), Apr 28-May 2 2023
sources.method: Ranked by net score (Eminem and Snoop tied 25, Kendrick 24, LL 23, Ice Cube 22, Drake and Tupac 20, 50 Cent 19...). Only 20 pre-selected rappers were rated, so for rappers outside that pool this source is skipped instead of penalised (my deviation from the missing-item rule).

sources.name: Billboard and Vibe 50 Greatest Rappers (editors, 2023), used ONLY to break ties
sources.method: Tie-breaks only: Jay-Z over Kanye, Ice Cube over Dr. Dre. Ranks beyond the top 10 come from the order of images on https://www.billboard.com/lists/best-rappers-all-time/ and are not verified.

changes_vs_current: Out (6): Rakim, Lauryn Hill, DMX, Method Man, KRS-One, Busta Rhymes; In (6): LL Cool J, Pitbull, Ludacris, Nelly, Future, Juice WRLD; Tupac falls from #1 to #4, Eminem rises to #1, Biggie falls from #2 to #16, Nas from #6 to #21.
confidence: low. Data is thin and splits two ways: streaming and sales data (Spotify, RIAA, Billboard) favour Drake, Kanye, Wayne and Travis Scott, while the pick and likability polls favour Eminem, Snoop, Tupac, LL, Ice Cube and 50 Cent. I added one rule of my own: a rapper needs at least 2 people-sources to rank in positions 1-21. Without it the strict method would put Travis Scott, Future, Juice WRLD, XXXTentacion and 21 Savage (Spotify-only) into the top 15. Positions 22-24 (Travis Scott, Future, Juice WRLD) have only Spotify behind them; their averages (12.0, 12.75, 13.0) are lower than positions 16-21, so avg_rank is not monotonic there. Top 10 passes the party test, but Biggie at #16 and Nas at #21 look too low (Biggie ranks 6th in Family Feud and 11th in YouGov but 37th on Spotify and has no sales data), Pitbull at #15 looks off, and Jay-Z has no Spotify data. Only one true pick-survey exists (Family Feud, 100 people, top 8). Ranker blocked.
